title: Construction begins on the Qin royal mausoleum
summary: Work began on the mausoleum associated with Qin Shihuang in the third century BCE. Its immense complex included burial structures and the terracotta figures later found near present-day Xi’an.

claims.text: Work began on the mausoleum associated with Qin Shihuang in the third century BCE. Its immense complex included burial structures and the terracotta figures later found near present-day Xi’an.
The source gives 246 BCE for the start; year precision does not imply a known day.

The mausoleum reveals how power could mobilize labour and craft production at great scale. The construction start is distinct from the emperor’s later unification of China and from the modern archaeological discovery.
